implementation_notes: In Swift the common case needs no clone at all: structs and enums are value types, so assignment, argument passing and return already hand you an independent copy (arrays, strings and dictionaries use copy-on-write, which is why large values stay cheap). A prototype is therefore just a configured struct value: assign it, mutate the fields you need on the copy, and keep the original untouched. For class hierarchies copying is not automatic, so implement an init(copy: Self)-style initializer or NSCopying when a clone must travel through a base type.
pitfalls: Value semantics is shallow for reference-type fields: a struct holding a class instance shares that instance, so deep copy still needs init(copy:) that copies the referenced objects.
Casting a struct to Any or boxing it (Array/NSArray bridging, @objc protocols) can reintroduce reference semantics and share state unexpectedly.
Copying a struct that owns a large class-backed buffer shares storage until mutated; custom copy-on-write via isKnownUniquelyReferenced must be implemented deliberately.

variants.name: class hierarchy + NSCopying.copy(with:)
variants.implementation_notes: For class hierarchies that must be copied polymorphically - and for anything bridged to Objective-C (NSDictionary keys, `copy` properties) - conform to NSCopying and implement copy(with:), returning a new instance carrying the receiver's values; subclasses override it and call the superclass implementation so inherited state is copied too. The return type is Any because the protocol predates instancetype, so callers cast. A Swift-native alternative is a Copyable-style initializer init(copy: Self) in a protocol, which keeps the static type without the cast.
pitfalls: A subclass that does not override copy(with:) silently produces a base-class copy and loses its own fields.
copy(with:) returns Any, so every call site casts (as! Shape) and the compiler cannot check the type.
Copying referenced properties is not automatic: the implementation must decide depth for nested class instances and call copy() on them where independence is required.
